div-short.why: Short division carries the remainder from each digit into the next, which is just place value again: a leftover ten becomes ten ones for the next column.
traps: Write the carried remainder down. Holding it in your head across four digits is where it gets lost.

div-long.why: Long division is estimate, multiply, subtract, bring down — repeated. The estimating is the hard part, and it is the same skill as approximating, which is why rounding practice pays off here.
traps: If a subtraction leaves a number larger than the divisor, your estimate was too small. Fix it before moving on.

div-remainder-meaning.why: The arithmetic is the easy half. The real question is what the remainder means: ignore it (complete bunches), round up (buses needed), report it (sweets left over), or convert it to a fraction. The same division gives four different answers depending on the question.
traps: 'How many buses?' always rounds up. 101 people in 50-seat buses needs 3 buses, not 2.02.

code.body:
17 // 5   # 3  — the quotient, rounded down
17 %  5   # 2  — the remainder
-(-17 // 5)  # 4 — rounding up
code.note: Most languages give you both halves separately: ~//~ for the quotient and ~%~ for the remainder.
